*Widget Forge* is a _small_ tool for building `{project}` widgets from plain text.
It runs anywhere, ships as one binary, and the current release is *{version}*.
The {unknown} reference stays as written, and snake_case_names stay plain.

toc::[]

== Installation

Grab a release from {repo}/releases[the releases page] or build from source:

[source,shell]
----
cargo install widget-forge
widget-forge --version
----

NOTE: The minimum supported Rust version is 1.85.

.Building from a checkout
[source,rust]
----
fn main() {
    println!("hello, widgets");
}
----

== Usage

Run the tool with a single input file:

 widget-forge build widgets.txt
 widget-forge check widgets.txt

Options are read from the command line first, then from the config file.
Press kbd:[Ctrl+C] to stop a running build. +
That line break above was a hard break.

=== Commands

* `build` compiles widgets
** writes into `target/` by default
** respects `+--out+` when given
* `check` validates without writing
* `fmt` reformats the input

. Write a widget file
. Run `widget-forge check`
.. Fix any reported errors
.. Run the check again
. Run `widget-forge build`

=== Progress

* [x] Parser
* [x] Renderer
* [ ] Plugin system

=== Configuration

build.out:: Output directory for compiled widgets.
build.jobs:: Number of parallel jobs.
Defaults to the CPU count.
log.level::
  One of `error`, `warn`, `info` or `debug`.

[TIP]
====
Keep the config file next to the widget sources so relative paths resolve
the way you expect.
====

WARNING: Version 2 changes the file format. Pin to *1.x* if you depend on it.

[CAUTION]
Deleting the cache directory forces a full rebuild.

== Examples

.A minimal widget
====
A widget file is a list of `name = value` lines.
Comments start with `#`.
====

.Sample output
....
widget-forge 1.4.0
  built 12 widgets in 0.4s
....

****
Sidebar: the format was inspired by INI files, but stricter about quoting.
****

[quote, Ada Lovelace, Notes on the Analytical Engine]
____
The engine might compose elaborate and scientific pieces of music.
____

////
This whole block is a comment and never appears.
It can span many lines.
////

[[windows-notes]]
=== Windows notes

Paths use backslashes, so escape them in config files: `C:\\widgets`.
Water is H~2~O and two to the tenth is 2^10^.
Some text is #highlighted# for emphasis, and **un**constrained bold works mid-word.
